thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Point To Lower Open After Jobs Report, Trade Talks Remain In Focus

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Point To Lower Open After Jobs Report, Trade Talks Remain In Focus
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer and Sara Sjolin, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Alibaba, Apple, GoPro, ShakeShack stocks could be active
U.S. stock-index futures pointed to a lower open on Friday, extending the recent weakness that has been seen in the equity market as the April jobs report came in below expectations.
Trade talks between the U.S. and China were also drawing attention, as the second day of discussions took place. The U.S. has reportedly handed Beijing's team a lengthy list of demands aimed at cutting the trade imbalance between the two.
What did the main benchmarks do?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 103 points, or 0.4%, to 23,806, while S&P 500 futures slipped 10.30 points, or 0.4%, to 2,621.25. Nasdaq-100 futures fell 31.50 points, or 0.5%, to 6,633.
On Thursday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-poised-for-mild-bounce-with-tesla-in-focus-2018-05-03), the Dow Jones Industrial Average recovered from a decline of as many as 394 points and closed up less than 0.1%, to 23,930.15, ending a four-session slide. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-on-track-to-close-at-a-six-week-low-2018-05-03)The S&P 500 index dropped 0.2% to 2,629.75, and the Nasdaq Composite Index closed 0.2% lower at 7,088.15.
For the week, the Dow industrials were set for a 1.6% slide as of Thursday's close, while the S&P 500 was looking at a 1.5% fall and the Nasdaq at a 0.4% decline.
What's driving markets?
The U.S. created 164,000 new jobs in April, below the 188,000 that had been expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-164000-jobs-in-april-unemployment-falls-to-39-2018-05-04). Separately, the unemployment rate fell to 3.9% from 4.1%, the first time the jobless rate has dropped below 4% since the end of 2000.
In Beijing, U.S. and Chinese officials were meeting for discussions on tariffs and other trade issues. Worries about trade hostilities between the top two global economies have roiled financial markets in recent months.
Read:Here's how sensitive the stock market has become to 'trade war' talk (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-investors-are-overreacting-to-trade-war-threat-these-charts-say-2018-05-03)
The U.S. has handed China a lengthy list of demands, The Wall Street Journal reported, including a demand to reduce the bilateral trade deficit by at least $200 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-seeks-200-bln-cut-in-china-trade-imbalance-2018-05-04) by the end of 2020. The deficit stood at $375 billion last year.
Several Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to speak on Friday. New York Fed President William Dudley kicks off the speeches at 12:45 p.m. Eastern at Bloomberg headquarters in New York, covering "financial tumult of our times and challenges ahead."
San Francisco Fed President John Williams is set to appear at a monetary policy conference at the Stanford University's Hoover Institution at 3 p.m. Eastern. At the same conference, Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Randal Quarles steps up at 5:30 p.m. Eastern to talk about liquidity regulation and the Fed's balance sheet.
Dallas Fed President Rob Kaplan, Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic and Kansas City Fed President Esther George are all slated to take part in a panel discussion at the conference at 8 p.m. Eastern.
What are strategists saying?
"We're at or near full employment, so the jobs report shouldn't be a big market mover, compared with issues like wages or trade. If we get through May and June and see that the trade talk was most rhetoric and posturing, that headwind will turn into a tailwind. Conversely, if this spitting match that is going back and forth leads to tariffs being enacted, then the headwind will become stronger," said Hank Smith, chief investment officer at Haverford Trust Co.
Which stocks are in focus?
Newell Brands Inc. (NWL) rose 4.9% ahead of the opening bell after first-quarter earnings beat forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/newell-brands-beats-profit-expectations-revenue-was-in-line-2018-05-04). The consumer goods company also announced an agreement to sell packaging maker The Waddington Group for about $2.3 billion.
Alibaba (BABA) climbed 2.4% premarket after the Chinese e-commerce giant posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and earnings that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alibaba-stock-gains-after-revenue-and-earnings-beat-expectations-2018-05-04).
Celgene Corp.(CELG) added 2.3%. The biotech company posted first-quarter earnings ahead of forecast and provided a 2018 outlook above analysts' expectations.
VF Corp. shares (VFC)may be in focus after the lifestyle and apparel retailer produced reported an adjusted profit that was better than expected and revenue growth of about 22% to $3.05 billion. Shares weren't actively traded.
After the close, Berkshire Hathaway Inc.(BRKA) (BRKA) is scheduled to release its quarterly earnings report. Chief Executive and Chairman Warren Buffett hosts Berkshire's annual meeting on Saturday.
Check out: How Warren Buffett's stock picks for Berkshire Hathaway have performed in 2018 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-warren-buffetts-stock-picks-for-berkshire-hathaway-have-performed-in-2018-2018-05-03)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-warren-buffetts-stock-picks-for-berkshire-hathaway-have-performed-in-2018-2018-05-03)Pandora Media Inc.(P) shares soared 12% ahead of Friday's bell after the streaming-music company late Thursday posted an earnings and revenue beat (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pandora-stock-rises-after-earnings-and-revenue-beat-2018-05-03).
Apple Inc.(AAPL) was up 1.1% after CNBC reported Berkshire Hathaway bought 75 million shares of the iPhone maker in the first quarter. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffetts-berkshire-hathaway-bought-75-million-apple-shares-in-first-quarter-2018-05-03)
CBS Corp.(CBSA) rose 2.6% after the media company late Thursday swung to a quarterly profit (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-swings-to-quarterly-profit-reports-sales-beat-shares-rise-2-2018-05-03) and reported a sales beat.
GoPro Inc.(GPRO) inched 0.8% higher before the open, after the technology company late Thursday posted earnings that beat expectations.
Shake Shack Inc.(SHAK) shares jumped 7.6% ahead of the bell. The burger chain late Thursday posted an earnings beat and lifted its outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shake-shack-shares-jump-after-earnings-beat-outlook-raised-2018-05-03).
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-find-cheer-in-china-talks-but-french-banks-pull-back-2018-05-04) were trading higher, while Asian stocks closed mostly lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/all-quiet-in-asian-markets-ahead-of-us-jobs-report-2018-05-03) ahead of the U.S. jobs report.
Gold prices inched down, while U.S. oil futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-turns-higher-as-dollar-moves-looming-decision-on-iran-sanctions-tug-at-market-2018-05-04) moved slightly higher. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index was up 0.1% at 92.539 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-springs-higher-as-us-jobs-data-take-center-stage-2018-05-04).
